thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Inch Higher As S&P 500 Tries For 4th Up Day In A Row

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Inch Higher As S&P 500 Tries For 4th Up Day In A Row
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
European Central Bank makes no change on interest rates
U.S. stock-index futures rose modestly on Thursday, suggesting Wall Street could extend its recent uptick to a fourth straight session.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures rose 105 points, or 0.4% to 26,118, while S&P 500 futures added 9.35 points, or 0.3%, to 2,897.75. Nasdaq-100 futures climbed 29 points to 7,515.50, a gain of 0.4%.
On Wednesday, the Dow closed up by 0.1% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stock-futures-inch-up-as-apples-iphone-event-grabs-the-spotlight-2018-09-12) and the S&P 500 gained less than 0.1%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 0.2%, as Apple Inc. shares (AAPL) lost 1.2% after the company unveiled new iPhones (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/everything-apple-just-announced-at-its-iphone-event-2018-09-12).
The Dow has risen for two days in a row, while the S&P has finished higher for three straight sessions. The three gauges have notched year-to-date gains of 5.2% to 15%, as of Wednesday's close.
Recent trading has been slight. The S&P 500 hasn't closed with a move of 0.5% in either direction any session thus far this month.
What's driving markets?
Investors continue to track the trade-related tensions between the U.S. and China, the world's two largest economies.
There is some optimism after a report late Wednesday that the Trump administration is giving Beijing another chance (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-offers-renewed-trade-talks-with-china-to-avert-new-tariffs-2018-09-12) to try to stave off new tariffs on $200 billion in Chinese exports. A fresh round of trade talks could take place later this month, and investors are optimistic that it could diminish the odds of a full-blown trade war erupting between the two.
While Wall Street has mostly shrugged off escalating trade tensions, with the S&P about 1% from record levels, analysts are concerned that the trade issue, if it worsens, could begin to act as a sizable headwind on growth.
Meanwhile, the European Central Bank made no change on interest rates, and said it doesn't expect any changes until summer 2019 at least. The ECB slightly trimmed its GDP growth forecasts for both 2018 and 2019, and ECB President Mario Draghi said that risks to the euro area's growth outlook were "broadly balanced."
Which economic reports are on tap?
The consumer-price index rose by 0.2% in August, its fifth straight increase (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/consumer-inflation-climbs-again-in-august-cpi-shows-but-pace-of-increase-slows-2018-09-13). Economists polled by MarketWatch had predicted a 0.3% gain. Separately, jobless claims fell slightly in the latest week, coming in at a 49-year low (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/jobless-claims-fall-slightly-to-203000-and-stick-to-49-year-low-2018-09-13).
At that same time, investors are due to get weekly jobless claims, with 210,000 claims expected.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic is due to speak about the economic outlook at an event in Jackson, Miss., at 1:15 p.m. Eastern.
What are market analysts saying?
"There are a lot of variables out there. Some are positive, like earnings growth, while others are negative, like the U.S. dollar. Those cross-currents mean there's been no real direction in either way, and it makes September something of a scary month for me, because there's a lack of earnings data and I'm worried the market can be dragged down on light volume because of news flow surrounding tariffs," said John Thomas, chief investment officer of Global Wealth Management.
Thomas noted that markets have recently been shrugging off tariff news, which he said was a cautious signal. "I wouldn't way we're becoming immune to the issue, but we brush it off more every day, and I'm worried markets underappreicate the impact it could have on large-capitalization companies that export a lot. Complacent is a good term for how things stand right now; everyone expects the market to continue going up, and that's a concern."
Which stocks are in focus?
Qualcomm Inc.(QCOM) rose 1.8% in premarket trading after it entered into a $16 billion accelerated stock repurchase program (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/qualcomm-sets-16-billion-accelerated-stock-repurchase-program-2018-09-13).
HollyFrontier Corp.(HFC) authorized a $1 billion stock buyback program (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/hollyfrontier-sets-1-billion-buyback-program-representing-up-to-8-of-shares-outstanding-2018-09-13).
Fred's Inc.(FRED) reported a drop of 3.5% in its second-quarter same-store sales (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/freds-same-store-sales-fall-35-loss-widens-2018-09-13). It also reported a drop in revenue and a loss that widened from the previous year.
Kroger Co.(KR) shares fell 5.6% in premarket trading after it reported its second-quarter results, which included same-store sales that rose less than expected (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/krogers-stock-drops-after-earnings-beat-but-sales-come-up-short-2018-09-13).
Pivotal Software Inc.(PVTL) reported results and a forecast that were generally better than expected, though the software company missed on billings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pivotal-software-stock-plunges-27-after-billings-miss-2018-09-13). The stock plunged 27% in premarket trading.
Shares of Acorda Therapeutics Inc.(ACOR) tumbled 19% before the bell. The company said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has extended the review period (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/acorda-shares-slide-19-premarket-after-fda-delays-review-of-parkinsons-treatment-2018-09-13) for a treatment for symptoms of Parkinson Disease.
Stock-market moves tied to Hurricane Florence (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/hurricane-florence-could-bring-catastrophic-flash-flooding-to-carolinas-virginia-2018-09-12) are likely to continue Thursday. Bojangles' Inc.(BOJA) has lost 7.9% this week as it is expected to be among the hardest-hit restaurant chains (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/restaurant-companies-at-greatest-risk-as-hurricane-florence-bears-down-2018-09-11), while retailer Home Depot Inc. shares (HD) have gained 5.6%.
